Opening (for podium, ~60–90s): Your Honor, this is not a garden‑variety performance dispute — this is a classic retaliation story: Jordan repeatedly raised an internal alarm about “cooked” sales numbers, and instead of investigating the truth the company labeled his concerns as “negativity” and then fired him; managers’ own emails flag his “pushback on reporting changes” and the termination letter explicitly blames “ongoing performance deficiencies and resistance to new reporting protocols,” language that mirrors the very conduct they say they punished, so what we have is the messenger punished for calling out cooked books — punished for telling the truth.  
Four‑point argument skeleton to return to: (1) Protected activity — internal complaints about manipulated sales figures; (2) Employer knowledge — contemporaneous manager emails noting Jordan’s “pushback on reporting changes” and “negativity around sales metrics”; (3) Causation — termination followed those complaints and used identical reporting‑resistance language; (4) Pretext — the company recast whistleblowing as “performance” and substituted a manufactured rationale in the termination letter.
